newsitem.title: USA: Chevron Q1 earnings reflect downstream gains. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Chevron Q1 earnings reflect downstream gains. [CORRECTED 17:20 GMT]

text.p: Chevron Corp reported higher first quarter profits on Wednesday, reflecting strong gains in the U.S. refining, marketing and chemical businesses.
The San Francisco-based company earned $831 million or $1.27 per share in the three months ended in March, up 35 percent from $616 million or $0.94 a share in the same period last year.
Revenues in the first quarter rose to $11 billion from $10.3 billion.

In a statement Wednesday Chevron attributed the higher earnings to a sharp rise in U.S. downstream and chemical operations, which benefited from lower costs of raw material lining oil and gas prices during the quarter benefited our U.S. downstream and chemicals businesses, as lower feedstock and fuel costs improved product sales margins," said Chevron Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Ken Derr.

U.S refining and marketing net earnings were $70 million. Excluding a special charge of $8 million, operating earnings stood at $78 million, a sharp rise from $18 million in last year's first quarter.

Chemicals net earnings were $63 million, about flat with $64 million earned in last year's first quarter. Results reflected the cyclical downturn in the chemicals industry, but were improved from year-ago levels because of lower feedstock, fuel costs, and price improvements for some products, the company said.

Despite declining crude oil prices in the first quarter, exploration and production earnings improved versus year-ago, reflecting a year-on-year increase in crude oil and natural gas prices, along with special gains.
U.S. exploration and production net earnings were $361 million, up from $268 million in the 1996 first quarter.
Results included special gains of $49 million from the sales of two producing properties and charges of $6 million for environmental remediation provisions.
Upstream profits alos reflected increased worldwide production and cost containment measures, Derr said. "Crude oil prices have continued to soften into the second quarter," said Derr.

"This should help maintain downstream and chemical margins, while our continued production growth and cost containment efforts should help lessen the impact of declining prices on upstream results," he added.
International exploration and production net earnings were $347 million, up 38 percent from $251 million in the 1996 first quarter.
First quarter net income was also lifted by $27 miilion from net special items.
